source: NCERT Class VIII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 6.

sections.heading: 1. Air Pressure and Winds
points: **Air exerts pressure** in all directions; **warm air is lighter** and rises, creating **low pressure**; **cool air is denser** and sinks, creating **high pressure**.
**Wind** = moving air; it blows from **high pressure to low pressure** areas.
The greater the pressure difference, the **stronger the wind**.

sections.heading: 2. Uneven Heating and Winds
points: **Uneven heating of the Earth** (equator vs poles; land vs sea) sets up pressure differences and winds.
**Sea breeze** (day, sea→land) and **land breeze** (night, land→sea) result from land and water heating/cooling at different rates.
The **monsoon** winds arise from uneven heating of land and ocean.

sections.heading: 3. Storms, Thunderstorms and Cyclones
points: A **thunderstorm** — strong winds, rising warm moist air, **lightning and thunder**, heavy rain.
A **cyclone** — a large, powerful storm with very **low pressure at the centre (the 'eye')** and violent circling winds; forms over **warm seas**.
Cyclones are called **hurricanes** (Atlantic), **typhoons** (Pacific) elsewhere.
A **tornado** — a dark, funnel-shaped, fast-spinning column of air (very destructive but local).

sections.heading: 4. Safety and Warnings
points: During a thunderstorm: **stay indoors**, avoid open fields, tall trees, poles, water.
For cyclones: the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** issues **warnings**; people evacuate to safe shelters.
Preparedness (early warning, cyclone shelters, evacuation) saves lives.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Warm air rises → low pressure; cool air sinks → high pressure; wind blows high→low.
Uneven heating (land/sea, equator/poles) drives winds & monsoon.
Cyclone = low-pressure storm with an 'eye', forms over warm seas; hurricane (Atlantic)/typhoon (Pacific).
Tornado = funnel-shaped spinning column; thunderstorm = lightning + heavy rain.
IMD issues cyclone warnings; safety = shelters & evacuation.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Warm air rises (low pressure)**; wind blows from **high to low** pressure.
A **cyclone** has a calm low-pressure centre called the **eye**.
Cyclones are **hurricanes** in the Atlantic and **typhoons** in the Pacific.
**IMD** issues weather and cyclone warnings in India.
